brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Seamline, the open-source command-line tool in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: precise, trustworthy, developer-native; it must work in a terminal-heavy README, as a GitHub avatar and on a small docs site. No database cylinders, no elephants, no generic terminal prompt. Web and GitHub only.

claim.notes: No concept passed the quality gate: overlap and split-s were struck at sketch review twice, and railstitch failed the blind gate in both rounds (brand-fit 5, distinctiveness 4-5, read as a 'D'), so nothing was finalized, exported or installed.

concepts.title: Overlap
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a generic app tile with a stepped line (toggle/slider glyph; stock 83%); s2 the letter L in a rounded square (wrong letter, stock 84%); s3 a git-branch/fork UI icon or a letter E (UI icon cliche); s4 a cracked circle / null sign (a break through a solid, exactly the tear/weak point the brief says to avoid; stock 84%). Every member is one cut through a stock container, so the shape that carries recognition is the square or circle, not the idea. Final round: direction ends.

concepts.title: Rail Return
readsAs: a bold letter D (or sideways P) led by a dash, '-D'
a magnet / U-shaped pipe bend turned sideways
a ':D' / '=D' grin emoticon or plug connector — unfortunate: a 'D' monogram for a brand named Seamline
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a dashed diagonal, staircase of stitches (closest to the idea, low stock 0.20); s2 two bars with a dotted seam, chart/signal-ish; s3 a seven-segment 5, a digit not an S: strike; s4 a '<' / git-fork glyph, branch cliche: strike; s5 a railway track or ladder, literal. Keep s1: the descending stitch-run is the only shape on all three boards that is neither stock geometry nor an initial. Fix: (1) it must not read as a loading/stepper indicator or a backslash of dashes, so give the run a defining rhythm (equal dashes, deliberate gap, maybe the run turns once) and tighten the 16 px render, where the dashes currently fragment; (2) the 'lit' dash in navy reads as off, not active: make the active step the brightest or invert the scheme; (3) shift the orange #E4572E away from red toward a clear amber/ochre, or go monochrome with one accent, and check contrast on light backgrounds.

concepts.title: Split S
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a blocky stepped S / mirrored Z / 5: the name's initial with a step, the stock monogram device; s2 the same S as a dashed outline: a broken or perforated S (reads as a tear line, which the brief forbids) and turns to noise at 16 px; s3 a script D or slashed O with a comet tail, i.e. a different letter, and its swoosh is too loose for 'precise, calm'. The thread-and-ring idea does not survive as a thread at 32/16 px. Final round: direction ends.
